Y is loaded from selected inventory slot $666F. Reject zero and the end index $667B through $09DF; a negative inventory byte returns without removal. Preserve the replacement block value at $08D3, classify the current map cell, replace its pickup representation through $09A5, and derive the inventory slot from the complemented block-class result. Extend the inventory bound if necessary, mark its description request, and increment the stored count with negative values treated as absent. For a negative request A, clear its high bit and set the later sprite-restore flag to zero; a nonnegative request sets that flag negative. Store the description request at $6994 and enter $0939 to present it.

Disable sprites, open the selected message window, wait for joystick fire to be released, and unless finished-game state equals one run the bounded input/delay helper with X=eight. Restore sprites if $0927 permits and clear elapsed movement counter $DC before returning.

Select request index $BD or $3D from A's sign. Patch the split description pointer at $6C7B/$6C3E from Y/X and enter the ordinary request-description path at $0928. This is a pointer override for one message slot.
Set Y=two, call the shared block/limit classifier beginning $4173, and enter $099B to return the current map cell's low nibble in A and its classification in X.

Call $4171 to update the player's map-column and block-limit fields, then use $AF to fetch the map cell low nibble and return block type $B0 in X. The secondary-object entry shares the final map read at $099B.

Record the map mutation through $58C8. Scenes eleven and twenty-three mirror the same change into each other's saved mutation records by temporarily substituting the scene index and calling $58DE. Restore the original scene, clear pending request $0530 to zero, and return. Other scenes still clear that request after the single mutation.

Mirror the change for the twin scene. If $0531 holds scene 11 ($0B), it is set to 23 ($17) while $58DE records the same mutation, then set back to $0B; if it holds 23, the roles swap. Any other scene skips this and goes straight to $09D0.
Write zero to pending scene request $0530 and return. This is the request produced after the Brick Hallway door-cell mutation, not a claim that the player travels to another room.
Store X in scene-entry field $0532 and Y in pending scene $0530, then return. This seven-byte helper changes the request without loading it immediately.
Load A with five and fall through into $09DF, which installs the text pointer from Y/X and uses A as the text indent value at $0342.

In negative map mode $0343, query the player cell through $0998 and accept translated type3 or2 by returning at $0A02. Otherwise select message $0D49, pull the helper caller's return address off the stack and tail-call $09DD, bypassing the rest of that command handler. At the natural column12 arrival, cell1 translates to type11 and fails this check. This is a command prerequisite, not proof that every other action or route is impossible.

For up to X groups of sixty decrements of $030E, watch keyboard-queue growth and joystick state $030C. A new keyboard byte is removed when it aborts the wait. Before returning, wait for joystick fire to be released, set the fire latch, and clear the wheel-prefix length; when $0927 is negative, also write zero to pending scene request $0530.

For each count in Y, set IRQ-maintained downcounter $030E to sixty and call $0A6D until it becomes zero, then decrement Y. Returns when the requested number of sixty-tick intervals has completed. The tick-to-wall-time rate depends on the running raster standard.
Store A into $030E and busy-wait until the IRQ service decrements it to zero. Unlike $0A27, this helper does not poll for an early input abort.

Initialize the resident display/IRQ services, set costume bases, and choose/load a save slot. Repeatedly service scene requests and costume rendering, wait for ten IRQ ticks, update object motion, service command wheels and the load-dependent room callback, then advance the random seed. The opening overlay is entered through the same resident load/menu path; its later callbacks retain their overlay-specific meaning.
Wait until the IRQ-maintained counter at $0353 reaches ten, clear it, and return. This paces the main graphical loop; it is not a disk-transfer wait.

Blank the display and, on first initialization, configure the processor port and call the initial $7900 loader. Disable interrupts, select port $25, clear workspace, copy initial hidden-RAM data, initialize sprites and screen, and install NMI/IRQ vectors. Reset sound, select the display bank/memory mode, enable raster IRQs, acknowledge CIA state, and disable the CIA timers through their control bytes. Enable all sprite slots before resuming interrupts and servicing sound. Subsequent entries skip the initial loader/copy according to $0F1D.
Clear zero-page bytes $10-$FF with an increasing Y loop. Processor port, stack and the lower zero-page fields are outside this loop.

Clear pages $0200/$0300, establish initial object order/buffer indices, mark four object/action entries inactive, and set display/message/input sentinels. Seed the keyboard queue with one $FD control, set queue length one, and mark room text modes $0343/$0344 negative. These are generated runtime initial values, not an imported screen image.

Operand byte of STA $02DF at $0FFF. The continuation of $0FB1 initializes keyboard queue length and its initial control byte, disables the scene marker mode, and marks room text-mode fields negative before returning at $1019.

Clear all 1,024 screen bytes at $CC00-$CFFF and all 2,048 bytes at $E000-$E7FF. Fill colour RAM with nine, then choose border/background/shared sprite and character colours. The $E000 range is generated cleared workspace in the opening snapshot, even though later scene resources can load a charset there.

Select port $24 so RAM under I/O/ROM is accessible. On the first initialization only, copy sixteen pages from $8BF8 upward into $E000 upward, incrementing the two self-modified high operands after each page. Restore port $25 and return. Later initializers overwrite portions of that copy, so retained bytes need their producer distinguished from the play-only consumer.

High-address byte of LDA at $107D, incremented for each page of the first-boot sixteen-page copy. The paired destination high operand at $1082 advances in parallel before the routine restores I/O visibility.

High byte of STA $E000,Y at $1080. The page-copy loop increments this byte and the source high byte after each 256-byte page, for sixteen pages, then restores port $25. This label is an operand inside $106E, not a new routine entry.

Clear $FF00-$FF7F, both pages $E800/$E900, and the 64-byte sprite at $FF80-$FFBF. Set that sprite's offsets ten and thirteen to $28. Select mode zero and clear the three allocated sets of seven sprite-strip buffers through $5AE8, reset projected sprite X bytes/high-bit state, and set VIC expansion/priority/collision and multicolour controls. The cleared/constructed sprite bytes are runtime output.

Clear scale input $12 and assign player/fourth-object costume bases $7900, with two other object bases $A000. If slot-menu state $63E6 is nonnegative, reset the selected disk-side cache and request side one through $5698; otherwise retain the loaded side. This sets bases without interpreting costume records.

Save A, X, and Y; select I/O with processor-port value $25; arm the raster chain through $1267; acknowledge VIC and CIA interrupts, update counters, and call frame services before restoring the saved banking and registers. The individual service purposes remain open.
RTI is the complete NMI target held in $FFFA/$FFFB in the opening snapshot.

Copy object render state, depth/colour fields, and display order into the raster service's zero-page slot arrays. Refresh sprite pointer sequences through $4984 when allocation/order changed. Copy the fourth-object colour to its pair and clear pending swap counter $63.
Set raster compare to $3D, install $127C in the hardware IRQ vector, clear the border color, and return.
